meta.title: Three-dimensional bioprinted glioblastoma microenvironments model cellular dependencies and immune interactions.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Rapid light-based printing built glioblastoma tissue with tumour cells, macrophages, astrocytes and neural stem cells in GelMA/hyaluronic acid. The model captured how macrophages support tumour growth and drug resistance.

formulations.review_notes: Print method inferred from the 'rapid 3D bioprinting' light-based system used by this group; confirm.
formulations.name: 4% GelMA + 0.25% GMHA (glioblastoma core)
formulations.cell_type: glioblastoma stem cells, macrophages, astrocytes, neural progenitors
formulations.key_outcome: Printed glioblastoma tissues reproduced tumour-macrophage dependencies and immune interactions.

evidence.quote: Cells were encapsulated into a material mixture of 4% GelMA (at 95% degree of methacrylation) and 0.25% GMHA
The stiffness of cell-encapsulated tumor core was 2.8 ± 0.6 kPa, while the less populated peripheral region containing NPCs and astrocytes was 0.9 ± 0.2 kPa.
